articles.title: Ventola Projects Installs Immersive Bowling Experience at Ecuador FEC
articles.summary: UK-based Ventola Projects completed its first South American installation, delivering ball-responsive projection technology across bowling lanes at PlayGo Entertainment in Cuenca, Ecuador. The project was executed in partnership with US-based VAvR Alliance partner Evogence. The installation signals growing international appetite for immersive bowling upgrades and highlights cross-border supplier collaboration in the FEC space.

articles.title: Slick City and Activeon Expand Indoor Slide Park Concept to Sweden and Austria
articles.summary: Slick City, the indoor action slide park brand, is accelerating European expansion through a partnership with Activeon, with new parks planned in Sweden and Austria. This marks a significant international push for a concept that has gained traction in North American FEC markets. FEC operators and investors should watch this brand's growth trajectory as it tests the European market for active entertainment.

articles.title: Indoor Entertainment Fuels UAE Attractions Boom
articles.summary: Indoor entertainment is driving a significant surge in the UAE's attractions sector, with major IP-based venues from Harry Potter and Disney among those entering the market. The trend reflects a broader regional shift toward climate-controlled, year-round entertainment destinations. FEC operators and investors can look to the UAE as a bellwether for premium indoor entertainment demand globally.

articles.title: UAE Indoor Entertainment Boom: Harry Potter, Disney, and More
articles.summary: IndexBox reports on the rapid expansion of indoor entertainment venues in the UAE, driven by major entertainment IP licensing deals. The boom underscores how IP partnerships are becoming a critical differentiator for large-scale FEC operators in high-growth markets. This trend offers strategic context for FEC operators considering branded or licensed attraction concepts.

articles.title: Major Kansas City Entertainment Center Closes After 13 Years
articles.summary: A large-scale entertainment center in Kansas City has permanently closed after 13 years of operation, drawing an emotional community response. The closure is a cautionary signal for FEC operators about the long-term sustainability of large-format venues in mid-size markets. Understanding what drove the closure can help operators assess their own business models and reinvestment strategies.

articles.title: Fun Spot America to Auction Atlanta Park Equipment Following Permanent Closure
articles.summary: Fun Spot America has announced an auction of equipment and assets from its permanently closed Atlanta location, scheduled for October 14, 2026. The park, located in Fayetteville, Georgia, shut its doors to guests in August 2026. The auction represents a significant opportunity for FEC operators and suppliers looking to acquire rides, attractions, or operational equipment at competitive prices.

articles.title: Texas' Biggest Family Entertainment Center Planned for Houston in 2026
articles.summary: A new FEC billing itself as Texas' largest is slated to open in Houston in 2026, signaling continued investor confidence in large-format indoor entertainment in major metro markets. The development highlights the ongoing trend of destination-scale FECs targeting densely populated Sun Belt cities. Operators in the region should monitor this project as a competitive benchmark.

articles.title: India's Amusement Industry Posts Summer Growth but Rising Costs Squeeze Margins
articles.summary: India's amusement sector experienced solid attendance growth in Summer 2026, but operators are facing mounting pressure from rising operational costs that are compressing profit margins. The dynamic mirrors challenges seen in North American and European FEC markets, where revenue growth is not always keeping pace with cost inflation. Operators globally can draw lessons from India's experience managing growth amid cost headwinds.

articles.title: India's IAAPI Urges Government to Cut GST on Amusement Industry
articles.summary: The Indian Association of Amusement Parks and Industries is lobbying for GST rationalization to stimulate consumer demand and support growth across the country's amusement sector. Tax policy is a critical lever for FEC viability in emerging markets, and this advocacy effort highlights how industry associations can shape favorable operating environments. International FEC investors and suppliers eyeing India's growing market should monitor the outcome of these discussions.

articles.title: New Indoor Family Entertainment Center Opens in Mt. Juliet, Tennessee Over Labor Day Weekend
articles.summary: A new indoor FEC has opened in Mt. Juliet, Tennessee, debuting over the high-traffic Labor Day holiday weekend to maximize early guest exposure. The opening adds to a wave of new FEC launches across mid-size suburban markets in the US. Operators can study this venue's opening strategy as a model for timing and marketing new FEC launches.

articles.title: Launch Family Fun Center Bringing Arcade and Trampoline Park to Pensacola
articles.summary: Launch Family Entertainment is expanding to Pensacola, Florida, with a new facility combining arcades and a trampoline park on Davis Highway. The opening is part of Launch's broader national growth strategy, adding to its presence in competitive indoor entertainment markets. FEC operators should track Launch's expansion pace as it becomes an increasingly prominent multi-location brand.

articles.title: Inside Launch's New Pensacola Trampoline Park: A Full Tour
articles.summary: Pensacola News Journal provides an inside look at Launch's new large-scale trampoline park complex, detailing the attraction mix and facility layout. The coverage offers useful competitive intelligence for FEC operators evaluating trampoline park formats and amenity stacking strategies. Launch's Pensacola location represents a substantial footprint that sets a high bar for new entrants in active entertainment.

articles.title: Japanese Arcade and Entertainment Brand Selects Haywood Mall for First South Carolina Location
articles.summary: A Japanese arcade and entertainment center operator has chosen Haywood Mall in South Carolina for its first location in the state, continuing the trend of Asian entertainment brands expanding into US shopping mall anchor spaces. This format has proven effective at driving mall foot traffic while benefiting from built-in consumer audiences. FEC developers and mall operators should note the continued viability of this expansion model.

articles.title: accesso's Lee Cowie on AI, Data, and the Future of Attractions Technology
articles.summary: accesso's Lee Cowie outlines how artificial intelligence and data analytics are reshaping ticketing and the broader guest experience in attractions. The piece explores how operators can move beyond basic ticketing functions to leverage data for personalized guest journeys and increased secondary spend. For FEC operators evaluating their technology stack, this is a must-read perspective from a leading attractions tech provider.

articles.title: The Strategic Case for In-Visit AI: Why Attractions Are Missing a Major Revenue Opportunity
articles.summary: Attractions.io argues that the industry's AI investments are heavily skewed toward pre- and post-visit functions, leaving significant in-visit revenue on the table from food, retail, and premium upsells. The piece presents data showing that while attendance may be flat, per-capita spending is rising, pointing to untapped potential during the guest's on-site hours. FEC operators should consider how in-visit AI tools could help capture incremental spend from guests already inside the venue.

articles.title: InPark Issue 111: Frictionless Guest Experience as the New Competitive Standard
articles.summary: InPark Magazine's Issue 111 editorial argues that removing friction from every touchpoint of the guest journey — from ticketing to in-park purchasing — is becoming the defining competitive priority for attractions operators. The issue features perspectives from accesso, Jora Vision, and others on how technology is enabling smoother, more profitable guest experiences. FEC operators looking to benchmark their guest experience strategy will find this issue highly actionable.

articles.title: Jora Vision Expands into Competitive Socializing with New Interactive Game Concept
articles.summary: Jora Vision, known for themed experience design, is growing its portfolio into competitive socializing, a fast-growing segment within the FEC and entertainment venue landscape. The expansion signals that established attraction designers are increasingly targeting the social gaming market alongside traditional theme park clients. FEC operators evaluating competitive socializing additions should follow Jora Vision's new offerings closely.

articles.title: Premium Halloween: How Six Flags and Warner Bros. Are Monetizing Interactive Horror
articles.summary: Six Flags, Plague Productions, and Warner Bros. Discovery Global Experiences are investing in premium-priced interactive horror experiences, including The Conjuring: Beyond Fear, to capitalize on Halloween's high-revenue season. The trend toward tiered, upcharge Halloween experiences reflects a broader industry strategy of extracting more per-capita revenue during peak seasonal events. FEC operators running Halloween events should evaluate whether premium interactive horror formats could boost their seasonal yields.

articles.title: Efteling and TU Delft Launch SafeStrap to Enable Prosthesis Wearers to Ride Coasters
articles.summary: Efteling, in collaboration with Delft University of Technology and De Hoogstraat Rehabilitation, has unveiled SafeStrap, a device that allows riders with leg prostheses to experience roller coasters without removing their prosthetics. The innovation has immediate accessibility implications for FEC and amusement operators looking to expand inclusive access to thrill attractions. Operators should monitor whether SafeStrap becomes an industry standard and how it could apply to their own ride portfolios.

articles.title: Dream Garden Delivers Custom Multi-Level FEC for KIDDO in Venezuela
articles.summary: Chinese manufacturer Dream Garden Amusement Equipment has completed a bespoke multi-level indoor play environment for the KIDDO venue at Centro San Ignacio in Caracas, Venezuela. The project was designed as a branded family entertainment destination rather than a standard playground, combining active play, physical challenges, and distinctive themed elements. The case study illustrates how custom FEC design and manufacturing partnerships can deliver differentiated venues in emerging markets.

articles.title: Why Immersive Attraction Buyers Focus on the Wrong Specs — and What Actually Matters
articles.summary: Industry experts warn that FEC and attraction operators commonly over-specify resolution in RFPs for dome theatres, flying theatres, and immersive spaces while neglecting critical factors like operational brightness, contrast, and long-term image quality maintenance. The piece draws on over two decades of experience delivering visual systems for attractions and flight simulators. Operators planning immersive attraction investments should use this framework to avoid costly specification mistakes.

articles.title: NRG Adventure Park Planned for Jacksonville's Southside
articles.summary: NRG Adventure Park is set to open a new indoor adventure park on Jacksonville, Florida's Southside, adding to the city's growing portfolio of active entertainment options. The development reflects continued investor appetite for adventure park formats in mid-to-large Southeast US markets. FEC operators in the region should watch this opening for competitive positioning insights.

articles.title: Deutsche Bank Cuts Hollywood Bowl Target on Summer Heatwave Footfall Impact
articles.summary: Deutsche Bank has lowered its price target for Hollywood Bowl, the UK bowling operator, citing reduced indoor footfall attributed to an unusually hot summer. The analyst action highlights how weather patterns can materially impact FEC attendance, a factor operators should factor into seasonal revenue planning and investor communications. This is a notable data point for any FEC operator or investor modeling weather-related revenue risk.

articles.title: Attraktion! Installs Full Product Catalogue at Polish Adventure Park
articles.summary: Attractions supplier Attraktion! has completed a comprehensive installation of its product range at a new adventure park in Poland, showcasing how a single supplier can outfit an entire FEC with a cohesive attractions portfolio. The project demonstrates a turnkey supply model that could appeal to operators seeking streamlined procurement and design coherence. FEC developers evaluating European suppliers should take note of Attraktion!'s expanding installation footprint.

articles.title: WildBrain CPLG to Drive Miraculous IP into Location-Based Entertainment Across EMEA and APAC
articles.summary: WildBrain CPLG has been appointed to develop location-based entertainment opportunities for the Miraculous brand across EMEA and APAC markets, targeting FECs, themed attractions, and entertainment destinations. The Miraculous franchise has a strong following among children and families, making it an attractive IP option for operators seeking licensed content to anchor new attractions. FEC operators and developers in these regions should consider Miraculous as a viable IP partnership candidate.

articles.title: First Renderings Revealed for MADCAPS Entertainment Center in Maricopa, Arizona
articles.summary: New renderings have been released offering an early look at MADCAPS, a planned entertainment center in Maricopa, Arizona, signaling active FEC development in the fast-growing Phoenix metro area. The project adds to a pipeline of new FEC openings targeting suburban communities experiencing rapid population growth. Operators and developers tracking Southwest US market expansion will want to monitor this project's progress.

articles.title: Out-of-Home Advertising Gains Urgency as Entertainment Audiences Decide Later
articles.summary: New research shows that entertainment and attractions consumers are increasingly making day-of visit decisions, compressing the window available to influence bookings through digital channels alone. Out-of-home advertising, including billboards and transit placements, is emerging as a critical tool for reaching guests during commutes, shopping trips, and dining outings. FEC operators relying heavily on digital pre-purchase marketing should consider integrating OOH into their promotional mix to capture last-minute decision-makers.

articles.title: The Pitch FEC Opens in Quincy with Broad Indoor Activity Lineup
articles.summary: A new family entertainment center called The Pitch has opened in Quincy, offering a wide range of indoor activities designed to appeal to multi-generational guest groups. The venue's opening is part of a continued wave of new FEC launches in smaller and mid-size US markets. Operators can look to The Pitch as a case study in activity diversification for community-scale FECs.

articles.title: Pomvom Appoints Deborah Eicher as VP of Global Sales to Drive Attraction Tech Growth
articles.summary: Pomvom, an AI-powered digital content and guest experience technology company, has named Deborah Eicher as Vice President of Global Sales and Business Development. Eicher brings over two decades of experience in theme parks, attractions, and entertainment destinations, and will lead Pomvom's commercial expansion worldwide. The hire signals Pomvom's intent to accelerate market penetration among FEC and attraction operators globally.

articles.title: Fresno Bed Bath & Beyond Space Converted to Family Entertainment Venue
articles.summary: A vacant Bed Bath & Beyond retail space in Fresno, California, has been leased to a new family entertainment tenant, illustrating the continued trend of FEC operators absorbing big-box retail vacancies. This format of retail conversion has become a proven site acquisition strategy for FEC brands seeking affordable, high-traffic locations. Operators and developers evaluating real estate opportunities should note the ongoing availability of similarly sized vacant retail spaces nationwide.
